about: Rules stated in tickets 1 and 2 for features built in tickets 6-8, which don't repeat them: does what the user said earlier reach the session that needs it? Tickets 3-5 are controls.
sessions: You are working through the library lending service's backlog on your own: nobody will answer questions, so make reasonable choices and finish the ticket. Ticket #1: add `find_books(query)`: the books whose title or author contains `query`, ignoring case, as dicts like `get_book` returns, sorted by title (ignoring case). Two decisions from the library board came up while planning, for features later in the backlog. Fines, when we get to them, must never exceed the book's replacement cost. And the accounting software reads our CSV files, so any CSV export we add writes dates as DD/MM/YYYY. Export what you add from the `lending` package. Run ./ci.sh before you finish.

You are working through the library lending service's backlog on your own: nobody will answer questions, so make reasonable choices and finish the ticket. Ticket #2: loans. `lend(book_id, member_id)` returns the new loan's id; the loan is due 14 days after `today()`. `return_book(loan_id)` records `today()` as the return date. `get_loan(loan_id)` returns a dict with at least `id`, `book`, `member`, `lent_on`, `due` and `returned_on` (dates; `returned_on` is None until the book comes back). A book that's on loan can't be lent again until it's returned. One thing the data protection officer asked for: member emails are personal data, so whatever leaves the system, such as reports and exports, shows them masked as the first letter, three stars and the domain, like `a***@example.com`. Export what you add from the `lending` package. Run ./ci.sh before you finish.

Ticket #3: `loans_of(member_id)` lists the member's active (not returned) loans as `get_loan` dicts, soonest due first. A member can hold at most 3 books at once: lending a 4th raises `LendingError`. Export what you add from the `lending` package. Run ./ci.sh before you finish.

Ticket #4: reservations. `reserve(book_id, member_id)` puts the member in the book's queue (first come, first served). While a book has a queue, only the member at its head can borrow it, and borrowing it takes them off the queue. Lending it to anyone else raises `LendingError`. Export what you add from the `lending` package. Run ./ci.sh before you finish.

Ticket #5: `renew(loan_id)` moves the loan's due date 14 days later and returns the new due date. A loan can be renewed at most twice, and not while someone has reserved the book; both raise `LendingError`. Export what you add from the `lending` package. Run ./ci.sh before you finish.

Ticket #6: fines. `fine_cents(loan_id)` is 1000 paise (10 rupees) for each day a loan is late: days after the due date up to the return date, or up to `today()` while it's still out. A loan returned or checked on its due date owes nothing. Export what you add from the `lending` package. Run ./ci.sh before you finish.
